rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command forbids turning attention from the poor believers toward worldly people; its purpose is to prevent scorning them for their shabby condition.
rows.anchor: والمراد النهي عن احتقارهم وصرف النظر عنهم لرثاثة حالهم إلى غيرهم

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: He reads عدا as “turn away,” with the verb taking the person or thing turned from as its second complement through عن.
rows.anchor: عداه عن الأمر عدوا وعدوانا صرفه واختار هذا أبو حيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative lexical construction gives عدا one object with عن, meaning to pass over or leave something.
rows.anchor: عدا الأمر وعنه جاوزه وتركه وجوز أن يكون معنى الآية على ذلك

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib says عدا intrinsically means passing beyond; Zamakhshari therefore supplies the sense of recoiling or rising above the object to explain عن.
rows.anchor: إن عدا حقيقة معناه تجاوز كما صرح به الراغب

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari argues that the wording combines leaving the believers and recoiling from them, a stronger effect than a single sense.
rows.anchor: ارتكب التضمين ليعطى الكلام مجموع معنيين وذلك أقوى من إعطاء معنى فذ

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan objects that Arabic-style verb inclusion is not analogical and should be used only from necessity when the ordinary lexical sense works.
rows.anchor: بأن التضمين لا ينقاس عند البصريين وإنما يذهب إليه عند الضرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The further objection that a semantic synonym must share the same transitivity is not compelling; the lexicon supports the alternative reading.
rows.anchor: لا يلزم من اتحاد الفعلين في المعنى اتحادهما في التعدية

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads the verb lightly as أعداه, with the eyes as an accusative object.
rows.anchor: بضم التاء وسكون العين وكسر الدال المخففة من أعداه ونصب العينين

rows.speaker: عيسى والأعمش
rows.claim: Isa and al-Aʿmash read the doubled verb عَدَّاهُ, likewise with the eyes in the accusative.
rows.anchor: بضم التاء وفتح العين وتشديد الدال المكسورة من عداه يعديه ونصب العينين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري وصاحب اللوامح
rows.claim: They treat the hamza and doubling in these readings as causative morphology.
rows.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري وصاحب اللوامح الهمزة والتضعيف للتعدية

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says that analysis fails: since the base verb already takes an object, causative morphology should yield two objects, which these readings lack.
rows.anchor: بل الهمزة والتضعيف في هذه الكلمة لموافقة أفعل وفعل للفعل المجرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Seeking worldly adornment” means seeking the company of wealthy worldly people unlike the poor believers.
rows.anchor: أي تطلب مجالسة من لم يكن مثلهم من الأغنياء وأصحاب الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the canonical reading the clause is circumstantial, most naturally attached to the eyes in عيناك; the genitive relation can license that attachment.
rows.anchor: وجازت الحال منه لأنه جزء المضاف إليه والعامل على ما قيل معنى الإضافة

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf assigns the circumstantial clause to the preceding verb, as in the construction بل ملة إبراهيم حنيفا.
rows.anchor: وقال في الكشف : العامل الفعل السابق كما تقرر في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular “you seek” can be attributed to the eye as a metonym for its owner’s desire; it may also mean looking for play rather than reflection.
rows.anchor: بأن إرادتها كناية عن إرادة صاحبها ألا ترى إلى ما شاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eye is treated as singular because perception is one, to signal its rhetorical insertion, or because the paired eyes are one bodily organ.
rows.anchor: إما لاتحاد الإحساس أو للتنبيه على مكان الإقحام أو للإكتفاء بأحدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds the ordinary circumstantial reading sound under either explanation of تعد; objections to a circumstantial clause from a genitive are too weak to displace it.
rows.anchor: ولا يخفى أن نية عدو لا عن الظاهر من غير داع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some assign the clause to the genitive only when تعد means passing beyond, and to the governing noun when it means turning away; the author sees this as stylistic preference.
rows.anchor: خص بعضهم كونها حالا من المضاف إليه على التقدير الأول وكونها حالا من المضاف على التقدير الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If turning away is meant, attaching desire to the eye keeps the sentence’s beginning and end parallel and avoids directly attributing worldly desire to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: فناسب إسناد الارادة إليها في آخره ليكون أول الكلام وآخره على طرز واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the two anomalous readings, the clause is circumstantial from the hidden subject of the verb.
rows.anchor: وهي على القراءتين الشاذتين حال من فاعل الفعل المستتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do not obey” prohibits removing the poor from the Prophet’s gathering at the urging of the heedless elite.
rows.anchor: ولا تطع ( في تنحية الفقراء عن مجلسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the elite’s hearts wholly unprepared for remembrance; their heedlessness contrasts with the poor who invoke God morning and evening.
rows.anchor: لبطلان استعداده للذكر بالمرة كأولئك الذين يدعونك إلى طرد الفقراء

rows.speaker: المفضل
rows.claim: Al-Mufaddal interprets remembrance here as the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الذكر ظاهر وفسره المفضل بالقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s apparent wording supports the Sunni doctrine that God makes the heart heedless; Muʿtazilites reinterpret it.
rows.anchor: والآية ظاهرة في مذهب أهل السنة وأولها المعتزلة

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The well-known Muʿtazilite interpretation takes “We made his heart heedless” as God’s abandonment or withdrawal of aid.
rows.anchor: فقيل المراد أغفلنا قلبه بالخذلان وهذا هو التأويل المشهور عندهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interpreting the phrase as “We found him heedless” is objectionable because it suggests God stumbled upon the state without prior knowledge.
rows.anchor: وتعقب بأنه لا ينبغي أن يتجرأ على تفسير فعل أسنده الله تعالى إليه بالمصادفة

rows.speaker: الكميت
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the verb as “attributed heedlessness to him,” illustrated by al-Kumayt’s line about people calling him wrong or sinful.
rows.anchor: قول الكميت : وطائفة قد أكفروني بحبكم وطائفة قالوا مسيء ومذنب

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummani says God did not mark the heart with remembrance as a sign of faith, using the image of an unmarked animal; the author calls it subtle but contrary to the apparent sense.
rows.anchor: المراد لم نسم قلبه بالذكر ولم نجعله من القلوب التي كتبنا في الايمان

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They argue that “he followed his desire” assigns the act to the servant, and that a divinely caused sequence should have used a causal فَـ.
rows.anchor: حيث أسند اتباع الهوى إلى العبد فيدل على أنه فعله لا فعل الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human acts may be attributed to the servant through acquisition and power and to God through creation; omission of a causal particle can be rhetorically deliberate.
rows.anchor: يجوز إسناده إليه بالاعتبار الأول وإلى الله تعالى بالثاني

rows.speaker: عمر بن فائد وموسى الأسواري وعمرو بن عبيد
rows.claim: They read أَغْفَلْنَا with fatḥa on ف and ل and قلبه nominative, making the heart the subject: “we found it heedless.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن فائد وموسى الأسواري وعمرو بن عبيد ( أغفلنا ) بفتح الفاء واللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that reading, the sense is that God supposed them heedless, with remembrance of God used as a metonym for divine requital.
rows.anchor: والمراد ظننا وحسبنا غافلين عن ذكرنا له ولصنيعه بالمؤاخذة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says removing the poor might secure elite conversion, making a small injury preferable to the greater harm of continued unbelief.
rows.anchor: وفي عدم طردهم لزم ترتب ضرر عظيم وهو بقاء أولئك الكفرة على كفرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knew the elite would at most make a merely outward profession, insufficient reason to violate the honor of the righteous poor.
rows.anchor: علم أن أولئك الكفرة لا يؤمنون إيمانا حقيقيا بل إن يؤمنوا إيمانا ظاهريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may also have forbidden expulsion because humiliating early believers would alienate hearts, prompt recent converts to apostatize, and deter future entrants.
rows.anchor: فربما يرتد من هو قريب عهد بإسلام ويقل الداخلون في دينه بعد ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This potential damage to Islam outweighs leaving a small group of unbelievers in their disbelief.
rows.anchor: وذلك ضرر عظيم فوق ضرر بقاء شرذمة من الكفار على الكفر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains فرطا as waste and ruin.
rows.anchor: أي ضياعا وهلاكان قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd takes فرطا as having advanced past truth and right, leaving them behind.
rows.anchor: متقدما على الحق والصواب نابذا له وراء ظهره

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya allows فرطا to mean either neglect and waste of religion or excess and extravagance; Muqatil likewise glosses it as extravagance.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون الفرط بمعنى التفريط والتضييع

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil explains the word as excess and extravagance.
rows.anchor: وبالإسراف فسره مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the elite “those whose hearts We made heedless” signals that their heedlessness and appetite explain why they must not be obeyed.
rows.anchor: للإيذان بعلية ما فيه حيز الصلة للنهي عن الإطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The truth is from your Lord” has an omitted subject, “this revealed thing is the truth”; “from your Lord” is preferably an emphatic circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: خبر مبتدأ محذوف أي هذا الذي أوحى إلى الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “the truth” is the subject and “from your Lord” its predicate.
rows.anchor: واختار الزمخشري هنا الأول قال في الكشف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to offer belief or disbelief is part of the Prophet’s statement and threatens listeners after establishing the revealed truth’s binding authority.
rows.anchor: من تمام القول المأمور به فالفاء لترتيب ما بعدها على ما قبلها بطريق التهديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat shows the Prophet does not depend on the elite’s promised conversion, which they conditioned on expelling the believers.
rows.anchor: وإظهار الاستغناء عن متابعتهم التي وعدوها في طرد المؤمنين

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf favors the omitted subject because it joins the thought tightly to the preceding command to remain with sincere worshippers and ignore worldly adornment.
rows.anchor: لأنه لما أمره سبحانه بالمداومة على تلاوة هذا الكتاب العظيم الشأن

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari favors construing the preceding phrase with an omitted subject rather than making الحق the subject.
rows.anchor: واختار الزمخشري هنا الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under either construction, some identify the truth as the Qur’an, the view transmitted from Muqatil.
rows.anchor: قيل المراد أنه القرآن كما كان المراد من المشار إليه على تقدير كونه خبرا

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the truth as divine unity.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك : هو التوحيد وقال الكرماني

rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Kirmani identifies it as Islam and the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك : هو التوحيد وقال الكرماني : الإسلام والقرآن

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makki says الحق means that guidance and abandonment come from God, who guides or leaves whom He wills; the author dismisses this interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقال مكي : المراد به التوفيق والخذلان أي قل التوفيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parsing makes the belief-or-disbelief clause a divine threat following the Prophet’s commanded declaration, rather than part of that declaration.
rows.anchor: تهديدا من جهته تعالى غير داخل تحت القول المأمور به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On either parsing, this is not a literal command granting an ethically neutral choice to believe or disbelieve.
rows.anchor: وعلى الوجهين ليس المراد حقيقة الأمر والتخيير وهو ظاهر

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafaji calls the command to disbelieve a metaphor for abandonment and indifference, like telling someone to do as they please.
rows.anchor: ذكر الخفاجي أن الأمر بالكفر غير مراد وهو استعارة للخذلان والتخليه

rows.speaker: كثير
rows.claim: Kathir’s verse, “Do us wrong or treat us well; no blame,” illustrates the rhetorical show of indifference.
rows.anchor: أسيئي بنا أو أحسني لا ملومة

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Muʿtazilites infer human independence because belief and unbelief are made contingent on the human chooser’s will.
rows.anchor: واستدل المعتزلة بالآية على أن العبد مستقل في افعاله موجد لها

rows.speaker: الأشاعرة
rows.claim: The author replies that even if human will produces acts, it itself depends on God’s will, so independence fails; this is the Ashʿari position of humans compelled in the form of choosers.
rows.anchor: ومع هذا التوقف لا يتم أمر الاستقلال ويثبت أن العبد مضطر في صورة مختار

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali argues that although one feels able to act or refrain at will, one does not choose whether the will itself arises; both will and action follow necessarily.
rows.anchor: ولكن هل تجد من نفسك أنك إن شئت مشيئة الفعل حصلت تلك المشيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some establish non-independence from the scriptural dependence of human will on God alone, without the contested regress argument.
rows.anchor: بعضهم يكتفي في اثبات عدم الاستقلال بثبوت توقف مشيئة العبد على مشيئة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says this verse was abrogated by the statement that people will only will what God wills; the author says that is false if meant literally.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي : هذه الآية منسوخة بقوله سبحانه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reportedly glosses the choices as those God wills to believe or disbelieve.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه قال في الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi cites the Ibn ʿAbbas report from Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi.
rows.anchor: والرواية عن الحبر أخرجها ابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم والبيهقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the report is sound, Alusi says it explains human choices as accordant with God’s will rather than changing the grammatical subject.
rows.anchor: فإذا صحت يحتمل أن يكون ذلك القول لبيان أن من شاء الإيمان هو من شاء الله تعالى له الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically the subject is “whoever”; if Ibn ʿAbbas’s report is sound, it explains that the human chooser’s will accords with God’s, as the verse’s ending confirms.
rows.anchor: والحق أن الفاعل ضمير ( من ) والرواية عن الحبر أخرجها

rows.speaker: أبو السمال قعنب
rows.claim: Abu al-Sammal reads قل الحق with a fatḥa on the lām; Abu Hatim calls this poor Arabic.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال قعنب ( وقل الحق ) بفتح اللام حيث وقع

rows.speaker: أبو السمال قعنب
rows.claim: He is also reported to read the lām with ḍamma, apparently harmonizing it with the preceding قاف.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا ضم اللام حيث وقع كأنه اتباع لحركة القاف

rows.speaker: أبو السمال قعنب
rows.claim: He also reads الحق in the accusative, parsed as though the command said “speak the true statement.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ أيضا ( الحق ) بالنصب وخرجه صاحب اللوامح على تقدير قل القول الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من ربكم is variously parsed as a circumstantial phrase or as an adjective, with the adjectival analysis raising a grammatical question.
rows.anchor: قيل حال أي كائنا من ربكم وقيل : صفة أي الكائن

rows.speaker: الحسن وعيسى الثقفي
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and ʿIsa al-Thaqafi read both imperative lām particles with kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعيسى الثقفي ( فليؤمن وليكفر ) بكسر لام الأمر فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “wrongdoers” are those who disbelieve after the truth comes from God; naming them wrongdoers underscores their choice as transgression.
rows.anchor: للكافرين بالحق بعد ما جاء من الله سبحانه والتعبير عنهم بالظالمين للتنبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepared Fire either explains the threatening choice or reinforces the divine threat if the choice clause is itself from God.
rows.anchor: والجملة تعليل للأمر بما ذكر من التخيير التهديدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أعتدنا means “prepared,” from عتاد, or derives from أعددنا with one د replaced by ت.
rows.anchor: من العتاد وهو في الأصل ادخال الشيء قبل الحاجة إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire’s spreading flames around the unbelievers are likened to a tent enclosure; سرادق is a metaphor for its enveloping barrier.
rows.anchor: شبه به ما يحيط بهم من لهبها المنتشر منها في الجهات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations of سرادق include a tent’s surrounding curtain or rising smoke that encircles something; both are figurative here.
rows.anchor: السرادق الحجزة التي تكون حول الفسطاط تمنع من الوصول إليه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reportedly interprets the enclosure as the combination of flame and smoke.
rows.anchor: والمروي عن قتادة تفسيره بمجموع الأمرين اللهب والدخان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the enclosure is a wall of fire.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن ابن عباس أنه حائط من نار

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi describes it as a neck emerging from the Fire and encircling the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وحكى الكلبي أنه عنق يخرج من النار فيحيط بالكفار

rows.speaker: القاضي الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi says the surrounding sea will become fire on the Day of Resurrection and encircle them.
rows.anchor: حكى القاضي الماوردي أنه البحر المحيط بالدنيا يكون يوم القيامة نارا

rows.speaker: يلعى بن أمية
rows.claim: A report from Yala ibn Umayya says the Prophet called the sea part of Hell and recited this verse; the source notes that Ibn Abi Hatim authenticated it.
rows.anchor: عن يلعي بن أمية أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib says سرادق is a Persian loanword, but his claim that its consonant pattern is unattested in Arabic is refuted by several Arabic examples.
rows.anchor: وليس من كلامهم اسم مفرد ثالثه ألف وبعده حرفان انتهى

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Proposed Persian sources include سرايرده, “covering of the court,” and سراطاق, “arch of the court”; Abu Hayyan instead cites سرداد, meaning vestibule.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حيان وغيره : معرب سرداد وهو الدهليز

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: The masculine loanword takes a sound feminine plural, سرادقات; lexicographers define it as anything enclosing a place or shelter.
rows.anchor: ويجمع كما قال سيبويه بالألف والتاء وإن كان مذكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appeal for help is contextualized as thirst by the water that follows, though it may concern every kind of torment.
rows.anchor: من العطش بقرينة قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير
rows.claim: They describe the molten drink as thick liquid like the dregs of oil.
rows.anchor: على ما أخرج ابن جرير وغيره عن ابن عباس وابن جبير ماء غليظ كدردي الزيت

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: A Prophetic report likens the drink to oil dregs and says that when brought near, the face’s skin falls into it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: غير واحد
rows.claim: Other authorities identify the drink as molten substances from the earth or molten copper.
rows.anchor: وقال غير واحد : هو ما أذيب من جواهر الأرض

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud compares molten gold and silver to the drink’s appearance, while stressing that Hell’s drink is much hotter.
rows.anchor: هذا أشبه شيء بالمهل الذي هو شراب أهل النار ولونه لون السماء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the drink as pus and black blood; another view calls it a kind of tar.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد أنه القيح والدم الأسود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise that they will be given drink is sarcastic understatement, illustrated by Bishr ibn Abi Hazim’s line about being compensated with slaughter.
rows.anchor: خارج مخرج التهكم بهم كقول بشر بن أبي حازم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extreme heat will roast their faces and strip their skin; “faces” most likely means the actual facial organs, though it may stand for whole bodies.
rows.anchor: ينضجها إذا قدم ليشرب من فرط حرارته حتى أنه يسقط جلودها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يشوي الوجوه can modify the water as a second adjective or circumstantial clause, or be a circumstantial clause from the molten drink.
rows.anchor: والجملة صفة ثانية لماء والأولى

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some place يشوي الوجوه circumstantially with the hidden pronoun in كالمهل, but al-Khafaji objects that the particle is not an adjective able to contain a pronoun.
rows.anchor: لأنها ليست صفة مشتقة حتى يستتر فيها ولم يعهد مشتق على حرف واحد

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli al-Farisi likewise says it is difficult to make ذؤابتي the subject of كـ in the poetic comparison to a partridge’s nest.
rows.anchor: وذكر أن أبا علي الفارسي منع في شرح الشواهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “How wretched a drink” refers to the water they receive, and “how evil a resting place” refers to the Fire.
rows.anchor: ذلك الماء الذي يغاثون به

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والسدي
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda and al-Suddi explain مرتفقا as a place or posture for leaning on the elbow.
rows.anchor: أي متكأ كما قال أبو عبيدة وروى عن السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word derives from leaning on the arm’s elbow; مرتفقا may be a place noun used as a specification.
rows.anchor: وأصل الإرتفاق كما قيل الاتكاء على مرفق اليد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari calls مرتفقا a contrastive echo of “a good resting place” in 18:31, since Hell offers neither rest nor reclining.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري : وهذه لمشاكلة قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf argues reclining can express grief as well as comfort, so the phrase might be literal.
rows.anchor: أن الاتكاء على الحقيقة كما يكون للتنعم يكون للتحزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says punishment would occupy them too fully for literal reclining, so the phrase is mockery or a metonym for their lack of comfort.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن العذاب أشغلهم عنه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas interprets مرتفقا as a dwelling place; Qatada gives the same general sense.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أن المرتفق المنزل وأخرج ذلك ابن أبي حاتم عن قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAta glosses it as a place of settlement.
rows.anchor: وفي معناه قول ابن عطاء

rows.speaker: العتبي
rows.claim: Al-ʿUtbi glosses it as a gathering place.
rows.anchor: وقيل موضع الترافق أي ساءت موضعا للترافق

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains it as a place where people meet and associate; the author rejects al-Tabari’s denial that this sense is possible.
rows.anchor: وكأنه مراد مجاهد في تفسيره بالمجتمع فإنكار الطبري أن يكون له معنى مكابرة

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari reads the phrase as saying Hell is a terrible destination for someone seeking relief, since its seeker finds none.
rows.anchor: المعنى ساءت مطلبا للرفق لأن من طلب رفقا من جهنم عدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some parse مرتفقا as a verbal noun meaning reclining or seeking repose.
rows.anchor: وجوز بعضهم أن يكون المرتفق مصدرا ميما بمعنى الارتفاق والاتكاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening لولا rebukes the garden-owner and urges him to say this at the very moment of entering.
rows.anchor: حض على القول وتوبيخ على تركه وتقديم الظرف على المحضض عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما شاء الله may mean “the matter is what God wills,” or “whatever God willed has come to be”; it can be a relative or a conditional clause.
rows.anchor: أي الأمر ما شاء الله أو ما شاء الله تعالى كائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Either construction urges recognition that the orchard and everything in it exist by God’s will and may be preserved or destroyed by Him.
rows.anchor: فالمراد تحضيضه على الإعتراف بأن جنته وما فيها بمشيئة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ما is conditional or functions like one, the wording also implies that what God does not will will not occur.
rows.anchor: يفيد عدمه عند عدمه فيكون المعنى

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilite al-Qaffal restricts “what God willed” to the fruit in the garden, denying that the clause is universal.
rows.anchor: وزعم القفال من المعتزلة أن التقتير هذا ما شاء الله تعالى والإشارة إلى ما في الجنة

rows.speaker: الكعبي والجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Kaʿbi and al-Jubbaʾi say the verse covers only what God directly does, not human acts; things He dislikes may occur in His dominion.
rows.anchor: الآية خاصة فيما تولى الله تعالى فعله ولا تشمل ما هو من فعل العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author insists that the natural reading is universal and says the Muʿtazilites depart from that sense to protect their doctrine.
rows.anchor: أن المنساق إلى الفهم العموم وكم للمعتزلة عدول عن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “There is no power except through God” confesses the speaker’s inability and that his building and management depend on divine aid and empowerment.
rows.anchor: اعترافا بعجزك وإقرارا بأن ما تيسر لك من عمارتها وتدبير أمرها

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits the Prophet’s description of this invocation as a treasure of Paradise beneath the Throne; he distinguishes it from لا حول ولا قوة بالله.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال لي نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ألا أدلك على كنز من كنوز الجنة

rows.speaker: عمرو بن مرة
rows.claim: Ibn Murra says that a person’s saying ما شاء الله is among the best supplications.
rows.anchor: عن عمرو بن مرة قال : إن من أفضل الدعاء قول الرجل

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports a Prophetic promise that invoking the phrase over blessings in family, property, or children protects from every calamity until death.
rows.anchor: ما أنعم الله على عبد نعمة في أهل أو مال أو ولد فيقول ما شاء الله لا قوة إلا بالله

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas says that invoking the phrase when something in one’s property pleases the viewer prevents calamity from striking it; another version is Prophetic.
rows.anchor: من رأى شيئا من ماله فأعجبه فقال ما شاء الله

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik said ما شاء الله when entering his home, citing the verse; Ibn al-ʿArabi inferred that it is recommended when entering one’s home.
rows.anchor: كان مالك إذا دخل بيته يقول : ما شاء الله

rows.speaker: عروة
rows.claim: ʿUrwa said the phrase on seeing something pleasing in his property or entering a garden, applying the verse.
rows.anchor: عن عروة أنه كان إذا رأى من ماله شيئا يعجبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports support saying the invocation on seeing anything pleasing, one’s own or another’s, as protection from the evil eye of admiration.
rows.anchor: ويفهم من بعض الروايات استحباب قول ذلك عند رؤية ما يعجب مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ترني أنا أقل, أنا emphasizes the object pronoun; تراني may denote knowledge, taking أقل as its second object, or sight, making it a circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: توكيد للضمير المنصوب على المفعولية في ( ترني )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أنا can instead be a separator, in which case the seeing verb must be cognitive rather than visual.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ( أنا ) فصلا وحينئذ يتعين

rows.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
rows.claim: Isa ibn ʿUmar reads أقل in the nominative; أنا is then the subject and أقل its predicate.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بن عمر ( أقل ) بالرفع فيكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مالا وولدا are specification words on both readings.
rows.anchor: و ( مالا وولدا ) تمييز على القراءتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أحيط بثمره means that the known wealth of both gardens and their contents was destroyed; surrounding enemies is extended metaphorically to total destruction.
rows.anchor: أهلك أمواله المعهودة من جنتيه وما فيهما وهو مأخوذ من إحاطة العدو

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafaji describes the image as a representative metaphor: the garden’s destruction resembles a people surrounded and annihilated by an enemy.
rows.anchor: شبه إهلاك جنتيه بما فيهما بإهلاك قوم حاط بهم عدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says construing the image as metonymy is more apparent than the proposed kinds of metaphor.
rows.anchor: وجعل ذلك من باب الكناية أظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause coordinates with an omitted event, implied by context, before the destruction.
rows.anchor: والعطف على مقدر كأنه قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author infers that destruction occurred at night from فأصبح; alternatively أصبح may mean simply “became.”
rows.anchor: واستظهر أن الإهلاك كان ليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Turning over his hands” may describe repeatedly exposing both palms and backs, or placing one palm over the other and reversing them.
rows.anchor: أن يبدي بطن كل منهما ثم يعوج يده حتى يبدو ظهر كل يفعل ذلك مرارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hand-turning is a metonym for regret and grief, unlike the idiom “turn the matter inside out,” which means shifting among topics.
rows.anchor: فهو كناية عن الندم والتحسر وليس ذلك من قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase على ما أنفق links to the implied regret: he was grieving over what he spent.
rows.anchor: فالجار والمجرور ظرف له متعلق بيقلب كأنه قيل فأصبح يندم على ما أنفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepositional phrase may instead be a settled circumstantial modifier meaning that he turns his hands while grieving; calling it emphatic depends on treating grief and regret as synonymous.
rows.anchor: أي متحسرا على ما أنفق وهو نظرا إلى المعنى الكنائي حال مؤكدة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some distinguish grief as narrower than regret.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إن التحسر الحزن وهو أخص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads “his two hands are turned over”; on this reading, ما can be verbal (“his spending”) or relative (“what he spent”).
rows.anchor: وقريء ( تقلب كفاه ) أي تتقلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He regrets the expenditure in particular because it could have been saved or used for other interests, and he had thought the garden indestructible.
rows.anchor: كان ما يمكن صيانته عن طوارق الحدثان وقد صرفه إلى مصالحها

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafaji says the garden and trees were abruptly annihilated by a heavenly calamity, as indicated by the immediate “then morning found him.”
rows.anchor: إن الآية تدل على وقوع اتئصال نباتها وأشجارها عاجلا بآفة سماوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خاوية means fallen or collapsed; the garden’s trellises are supports on which vines grow, and the collapse came down upon them.
rows.anchor: والعروش جمع عرش وهو هنا ما يصنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grapevines may be singled out because they are the main planting, their destruction entails the rest, or their cultivation cost the most.
rows.anchor: إما لأنها العمدة وهما من متمماتها وإما لأن الذكر هلاكها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description makes a report that fire burned the orchard unlikely unless “garden” means the entire property and the phrase means general ruin.
rows.anchor: ثم هذه الجملة تبعد ما روي من أن الله تعالى أرسل عليها نارا فأحرقتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ويقول coordinates with يقلب; some allow it as a circumstantial clause with an implicit pronoun, despite the rarity of an affirmative present verb with circumstantial و.
rows.anchor: عطف على ( يقلب ) وجوز أبو البقاء وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden-owner remembers his brother’s admonition and recognizes that his associating partners with God brought the loss.
rows.anchor: كأنه تذكر موعظة أخيه وعلم أنه إنما أتى من قبل شركه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possibility is that his words constitute repentance and renewed faith, since regret over past shirk suggests he now believes.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون توبة من الشرك وندما عليه فيكون تجديدا للايمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects that repentance: regret at disbelief alone is not faith, and here he regrets losing his garden rather than shirk as sin; later context still shows denial of resurrection.
rows.anchor: لم يتحقق هنا من الكافر ندم عليه من حيث هو كفر بل بسبب هلاك جنتيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance for sin requires resolving not to return and regretting the act as sinful, as discussed in al-Mawaqif.
rows.anchor: إذا عزم على أن لا يعود وكان الندم عليها من حيث كونها معصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the statement is instead spoken on Judgment Day, as some exegetes say, renewed faith there is unanimously useless.
rows.anchor: إذا قيل إن هذا حكاية لما يقوله الكافر يوم القيامة كما ذهب إليه بعض المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable recalls the world’s beauty and rapid disappearance so listeners will not be deceived by it or turn away from the afterlife.
rows.anchor: لئلا يغتروا بها ولا يضربوا عن الآخرة صفحا بالمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the command asks the Prophet to explain the world’s remarkable condition, itself like a strange parable.
rows.anchor: أو اذكر لهم صفتها العجيبة التي هي في الغرابة كالمثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كماء begins a fresh explanation of the analogy, “it is like water”; construing it as the second object of ضرب is grammatically awkward.
rows.anchor: استئناف لبيان المثل أي هي كماء

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Hawfi makes the comparison an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, meaning “a striking like water”; the author rejects this analysis.
rows.anchor: قال الحوفي الكاف متعلقة بمحذوف صفة لمصدر محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plants mingle densely because water is plentiful, or the water enters the plants and makes them full and lush.
rows.anchor: أي فاشتبك وخالط بعضه بعضا لكثرته وتكاثفه بسبب كثرة سقي الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although ordinary usage would say water mingled with the plants, the verse reverses the relation to emphasize water’s abundance, as though it were the primary mass.
rows.anchor: للمبالغة في كثرة الماء حتى كأنه الاصل الكثير ففي الكلام قلب مقبول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هشيما means dry, fragmented vegetation, either an intensive passive form or a plural of هشيمة; أصبح may simply mean “became.”
rows.anchor: أي يابسا متفتتا وهو فعيل بمعنى مفعول وقيل جمع هشيمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take أصبح literally as morning, since heavenly calamities often arrive at night; the author says the verse only describes eventual drying.
rows.anchor: وتعقب بأنه ليس في الآية ما يدل على أن اتصافه بكونه هشيما لآفة سماوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cycle resembles 87:4–5, where God brings out pasture and makes it dark, dry debris.
rows.anchor: ﴿ والذي أخرج المرعى فجعله غثاء أحوى ﴾

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda says تذروه means “scatter it.”
rows.anchor: أي تفرقه كما قال أبو عبيدة

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says the wind lifts the debris.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش ترفعه

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: Ibn Kaysan says the wind brings it and takes it away.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان تجيء به وتذهب

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reads تذريه, a four-form variant of the same verb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود / تذريه / من اذرى رباعيا

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي والحسن والنخعي والأعمش وطلحة وابن أبي ليلى وابن محيصن وخلف وابن عيسى وابن جرير
rows.claim: These readers use the singular الريح instead of plural الرياح.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي والحسن والنخعي والأعمش وطلحة وابن أبي ليلى وابن محيصن وخلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison is not water alone but the whole scene: water-grown plants flourish, dry, and are scattered until they seem never to have existed.
rows.anchor: ليس المشبه به نفس الماء بل هو الهيئة المنتزعة من الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The فاء signals how rapidly the vegetation vanishes; another reading treats it as an explanatory فاء with an omitted period of flourishing.
rows.anchor: وعبر بالفاء في الآية للإشعار بسرعة زواله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has complete power over all things, including bringing creation into being and making it perish.
rows.anchor: من جملتها الإنشاء والإفناء ﴿ مقتدرا ﴾ كامل القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question addresses unbelievers; if read as seeking their leave to announce the news, it is deeply sarcastic.
rows.anchor: خطاب للكفرة وإذا حمل الإستفهام على الاستئذان كان فيه من التهكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural “we” either immediately identifies the speaker or signals that believers already know this news as well.
rows.anchor: قيل لتعيينه من أول الأمر وللإيذان بمعلومية النبأ للمؤمنين أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أعمالا is an accusative specification; it is plural because it means “workers,” whereas a source noun used as specification can remain singular.
rows.anchor: أما إذا كان مؤولا بإسم فاعل فإنه يعامل معاملته وهنا عمل بمعنى عامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative says أعمالا is a rare plural of عامل; some grammarians deny such plurals outside a few established words.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن أعمالا جمع عامل وتعقب بأن جمع فاعل على أفعال نادر

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Another proposal treats أعمالا as plural of عمل, meaning people possessed of deeds; the author finds this strained.
rows.anchor: جمع عمل ككتف بمعنى ذو عمل

rows.speaker: إرشاد العقل السليم
rows.claim: The passage contrasts unbelievers’ intrinsically good acts, which they admire and expect reward for, with their intrinsically bad acts that they mistakenly deem good.
rows.anchor: بيان لحال الكفرة باعتبار ما صدر عنهم من الأعمال الحسنة في أنفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their effort is wholly lost and void before God; “in worldly life” modifies their striving, since its failure is not limited to this world.
rows.anchor: أي ضاع وبطل بالكلية عند الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وسعد بن أبي وقاص ومجاهد
rows.claim: One transmitted interpretation identifies the people as Jews and Christians; their deeds include acts of worship whose rules were abrogated.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس وسعد بن أبي وقاص ومجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other identifications are monks who impose harsh ascetic exercises on themselves, and the Sabians.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الرهبان الذين يحسبون أنفسهم في الصوامع

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: When Ibn al-Kawwa asked about them, ʿAli reportedly said they were the Haruriyya, the Kharijites.
rows.anchor: عليا كرم الله تعالى وجهه عنهم فقال : منهم أهل حروراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says the next verse calls them unbelievers, unlike Kharijites who do not deny resurrection; the answer is that مِن can mean sharing only their misguidance, or ʿAli may have judged them unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأن من اتصالية فلا يلزم أن يكونوا متصلين بهم من كل الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors reading ʿAli’s attribution as a harsh allusion rather than a precise identification of the verse’s subjects.
rows.anchor: واستحسن أنه تعريض بهم على سبيل التغليظ لا تفسير للآية

rows.speaker: العياشي
rows.claim: A report cited by al-ʿAyyashi says ʿAli identified them as People of the Book who disbelieved in God and innovated in religion; it adds that the river people are not far from them.
rows.anchor: أولئك أهل الكتاب كفروا بربهم وابتدعوا في دينهم فحبطت أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This report supports the earlier reconciliation and indicates that the description extends broadly to unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وهذا يؤيد الجواب الأول وأخبر أن المراد ما يعمم سائر الكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause may answer an implied “who are they?”, explain الأخسرين, describe or substitute for it, or be an accusative rebuke; the last analysis fits poorly because its opening does not state the key loss.
rows.anchor: ومحل الموصول الرفع على أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف لأنه جواب للسؤال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doing a deed حسنًا means performing it suitably; they believe they work properly because they admire and invested effort in their acts.
rows.anchor: الاحسان الإتيان بالأعمال على الوجه اللائق وهو حسنها الوصفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The circumstantial clause may modify the subject of “went astray” or their “striving”; the first makes their misguidance coincide with their mistaken belief and better exposes their error.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين الوجهين أن المقارن لحال حسبانهم المذكور في الأول ضلال سعيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The similar forms يحسبون and يحسنون produce a pun-like transposition of letters.
rows.anchor: قيل والأول أدخل في بيان خطئهم ولا يخفى ما بين يحسبون ويحسنون من تجنيس التصحيف

rows.speaker: البحتري
rows.claim: Al-Buhturi’s line about the one who trusts in God and the one who seeks Him illustrates the sound-play.
rows.anchor: قول البحتري : ولم يكن المغتر بالله إذ سرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise is widely understood as God creating affection for believers in people’s hearts during worldly life.
rows.anchor: والمشهور أن ذلك الجعل في الدنيا

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits the Prophet’s report: when God loves a servant He tells Gabriel to love him, announces this in heaven, and affection is placed for him on earth.
rows.anchor: إذا احب الله تعالى عبدا نادى جبريل انى قد احببت فلانا فاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The merciful title fits a promise arising from mercy; the future tense suited the Meccan believers’ rejection and was fulfilled after migration as Islam strengthened.
rows.anchor: والسين لأن السورة مكية وكانوا ممقوتين حينئذ بين الكفرة فوعدهم سبحانه ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One occasion report says it was revealed for the Abyssinian migrants with Jaʿfar, promising them affection in the Negus’s heart.
rows.anchor: وذكر أن الآية نزلت في المهاجرين إلى الحبشة مع جعفر بن أبى طالب

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
rows.claim: Another report says the verse came when ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf, newly in Medina, grieved to leave his companions in Mecca.
rows.anchor: عن الرحمن بن عوف أنه لما هاجر إلى المدينة وجد في نفسه على فراق اصحابه بمكة

rows.speaker: البراء
rows.claim: Al-Baraʾ reports that the Prophet told ʿAli to ask for a covenant with God and affection in believers’ hearts, after which the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن البراء قال : قال رسول الله ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) لعلي

rows.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya says every believer loves ʿAli and his family.
rows.anchor: وكان محمد بن الحنفية رضى الله تعالى عنه يقول : لا تجد مؤمنا

rows.speaker: الإمامية
rows.claim: Imami authorities report the verse’s revelation for ʿAli from Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Baqir, supporting it with a saying attributed to ʿAli about believers’ love and hypocrites’ hatred.
rows.anchor: وروَى الامامية خبر نزولها في على كرم الله تعالى وجهه عن ابن عباس والباقر

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A report attributed to ʿAli says that force cannot make a believer hate him or wealth make a hypocrite love him; the Prophet said believers do not hate him and hypocrites do not love him.
rows.anchor: لو ضربت خيشوم المؤمن بسيفى هذا على أن يبغضنى ما ابغضنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Love for ʿAli in this interpretation means proper, non-exaggerated love.
rows.anchor: والمراد المحبة الشرعية التي لا غلو فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author doubts a poem about loving ʿAli, attributed to the Christian al-Rusaghni, is genuine; if the Prophetic report is authentic, it also shows the attribution is false.
rows.anchor: وانت تعلم أنه إذا صح الحديث ثبت كذبه واظن أنه نسبة هذه الأبيات للنصرانى لا اصل لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Across the reports, the general wording governs rather than being restricted to the specific occasion of revelation.
rows.anchor: ثم العبرة على سائر الروايات في سبب النزول بعموم اللفظ لا بخصوص السبب

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi says the affection is a reward in the afterlife, either in Paradise among facing companions or when deeds are displayed publicly.
rows.anchor: وذهب الجبائى إلى أن ذلك في الآخرة فقيل في الجنة إذ يكونون اخوانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future tense also suits an afterlife promise; the verse singles out affection because unbelievers will then hate, divide from, and curse one another.
rows.anchor: ولعلا أفراد هذا الوعد من بين ما سيولون يوم القيامة من الكرامات السنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise may comfort believers after the prior statement that every creature will come alone before God on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: لما اخبرا باتيان كل من أهل السموات والأرض اليه سبحانه يوم القيامة فردا

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya interprets the promise in this context as God’s love for them, meaning His honoring and forgiving them.
rows.anchor: وفسره ابن عطيه على هذا الوجه بمحبته تعالى اياهم واراد منها اكرامه تعالى اياهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse may promise affection both in this world and the next; the merciful title can apply generally to both realms.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون الوعد بجعل الود في الدنيا والاخرة ولا اراه بعيدا عن الصواب

rows.speaker: أبو الحرث الحنفي
rows.claim: Abu al-Harith al-Hanafi reads وُدًّا with fatḥa on the wāw.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو الحرث الحنفى ( ودا ) بفتح الواو

rows.speaker: جناح بن حبيش
rows.claim: Junah ibn Hubaysh reads وُدًّا with kasra on the wāw; both forms are dialectal variants of the word for affection.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جناح بن حبيش ( ودا ) بكسرها وكل ذلك لغة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience over their words is possible because delayed punishment is respite rather than neglect and will inevitably arrive; it means composure, not abandoning combat.
rows.anchor: من أن تاخير عذابهم ليس باهمال بل امهال وانه لازم لهم البتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading patience as a command to cease fighting would make the verse abrogated, but that is not intended.
rows.anchor: والمراد به عدم الأضطراب لاترك القتال حتى تكون الآية منسوخة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To glorify God with praise means to pray while praising the Lord who brings the Prophet to perfection through guidance and enabling grace.
rows.anchor: أي صل وانت حامد لربك عز وجل الذي يبلغك إلى كمالك على هدايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Before sunrise” means the dawn prayer and “before sunset” the sunset prayer; the time phrase most naturally modifies the command to glorify.
rows.anchor: أي صلاة الفجر ( وقبل غروبها ( أي صلاة المغرب

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: A Prophetic report from Jarir interprets glorification at these two times as the two prayers.
rows.anchor: وقد أخرج تفسير التسبيح في هذين الوقتين بما ذكر الطبراني

rows.speaker: فضالة بن وهب الليثي
rows.claim: The Prophet told Fadala to keep the “two ʿasrs,” explaining them as a prayer before sunrise and another before sunset.
rows.anchor: عن فضالة بن وهب الليثي أن النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام قال له : حافظ على العصرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative interprets the pre-sunset period as noon and afternoon prayers; both occur after noon and before sunset, although ordinary usage favors afternoon.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد بالتسبيح قبل غروبها صلاتا الظهر والعصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آناء means the hours or portions of the night; several spellings and forms are reported, with three more common than the form used here.
rows.anchor: أي من ساعاته جمع إنى وانو بالياء والواو وكسر الهمزة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib relates أناه to time in the verse about guests waiting for food, and cites poetry about delaying supper until a star rose.
rows.anchor: قال الله تعالى ( غير ناظرين اناه ) أي وقته

rows.speaker: الحطيئة
rows.claim: Al-Hutayʾa’s verse uses آنيت for delaying supper and الإناء for the delay.
rows.anchor: وآنيت العشاء إلى سهيل أو الشعرى فطال بي الاناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing makes “some night hours” a time phrase governed by an implied “rise,” with فسبح coordinated after it; the author finds this strained.
rows.anchor: قيل منصوب على الظرفية بمضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other parses make it govern فسبح directly, place it in coordination with وإياي فارهبون, or treat فاء as explanatory or additional for necessary sequence.
rows.anchor: وقيل : منصوب بسبح على نسق ( وإياي فارهبون )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading makes the night-hours phrase the object of فسبح and treats فاء as an added marker that the command necessarily follows.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنه معمول ( فسبح )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أطراف النهار may attach to the position of من آناء الليل, or to the earlier phrase قبل طلوع.
rows.anchor: عطف على محل قوله سبحانه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada, as transmitted by Ibn Jarir and others, interprets the daylight prayer as noon; al-Jubbaʾi prefers that view.
rows.anchor: والمراد من التسبيح اطراف النهار على ما أخرج ابن جرير وابن المنذر وغيرهما عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noon prayer is called an edge because it ends the first half of the day and begins the second, or because every day has two such edges.
rows.anchor: ووجه إطلاق الطرف على وقتها بأنه نهاية النصف الأول من النهار وبداية النصف الأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This explanation is strained: the boundary is outside one half but inside the other, the plural implies at least two, and neither half’s edge is the edge of the whole day.
rows.anchor: أن البداية والنهاية فيه ليست على وتيرة واحدة لأن كون ذلك نهاية باعتبار أن النصف الأول انتهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation repeats dawn and sunset prayers, taking the day as sunrise to sunset and its two ends as the points beside its beginning and end.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هذا تكرير لصلاتي الصبح والمغرب ايذانا باختصاصهما بمزيد مزية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural can denote two edges without ambiguity because the day has only two; matching the plural of night hours favors this reading.
rows.anchor: والمرجح المشاكلة لآناء الليل

rows.speaker: العجاج
rows.claim: Al-ʿAjjaj’s line uses a dual pair of deserts and their two backs as a poetic parallel for plural wording about two things.
rows.anchor: قول العجاج : ومهمهين فدفدين مرتين ظهراهما مثل ظهور الترسين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further option repeats dawn and afternoon prayers, with the daytime beginning at dawn; if it begins at sunrise, the two ends are not parallel.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون تكريرا لصلاتي الصبح والعصر ويراد بالنهار ما بين طلوع الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take the phrase as an order for voluntary prayer in the day’s final hours; this shifts away from the apparent meaning and that period’s suitability for prayer is debatable.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو أمر بالتطوع في الساعات الأخيرة للنهار وفيه صرف الأمر عن ظاهره

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafaji says the phrase is governed by the preceding verb without calling فاء additional, since it does not prevent a verb from governing earlier material.
rows.anchor: وذكر الخفاجي أنه معمول لما ذكر من غير حاجة لدعوى زيادة الفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night prayer here means the sunset and nightfall prayers; their special importance warrants a renewed command and foregrounding their hours.
rows.anchor: والمراد من التسبيح في بعض آناء الليل صلاة المغرب وصلاة العشاء
